newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to attend Hong Kong investiture -- Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: Japan to attend Hong Kong investiture -- Hashimoto.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Friday Japanese officials will attend the controversial inauguration of Hong Kong's unelected legislature on July 1.
"I know there is an issue over whether we should go to this or not," Hashimoto told reporters. "But I think we must go."

British Prime Minister Tony Blair and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will boycott the investiture ceremony of Hong Kong's appointed provisional legislature, which will replace the democratically elected assembly.
The event takes place after midnight on July 1, when Hong Kong becomes a special administrative region of China.
Japan has not yet announced its delegation but newspaper reports have said Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, and former prime ministers Tomiichi Murayama and Noboru Takeshita will attend.

Japan's ties with China soured last year because of a row over sovereignty of islets in the East China Sea, Hashimoto's visit to a controversial Tokyo war shrine, Japan's suspension of grant-in-aid after China's nuclear tests, and moves to expand Japan's military role within the U.S.-Japan security framework.

But in recent months the relationship has improved. In March Japan lifted the suspension of grant-in-aid and both countries agreed in principle to an exchange of visits this year by Hashimoto and Chinese Premier Li Peng, with Chinese President Jiang Zemin expected to travel to Tokyo in 1998.
